title: Overseas Tankship (UK) Ltd v Morts Dock (The Wagon Mound No 1)

content.caseIdentity: Overseas Tankship (UK) Ltd v Morts Dock (The Wagon Mound No 1), [1961] AC 388
content.facts: The kind of damage must be reasonably foreseeable; the precise sequence or manner need not be foreseeable.
questionsBeforeCourt: What legal rule governs the doctrine?
content.ratioDecidendi: Remoteness in negligence is reasonable foreseeability of the kind of damage, not the direct-consequence test. Fire damage from furnace oil on the water was not reasonably foreseeable on the findings. Citation already in this file: [1961] AC 388.
content.holding: The kind of damage must be reasonably foreseeable; the precise sequence or manner need not be foreseeable.
content.relevance: Use the case for the precise proposition it decides.
